answer.rationale: With 14 days to expiry, no auto-renew, and the line at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, a primary-vendor switch carries unacceptable delivery risk this cycle regardless of the unit-cost upside in memory_c2 — I want to verify c2 to check whether its sharp cost cut concealed downstream quality/delivery costs before ruling switching out entirely. Renegotiation at renewal (memory_c4) is the only lever that attacks the 18% mandate while keeping the stable incumbent integration (memory_c1, memory_c6); I verify c4 to confirm the benchmarking approach actually moved price and terms rather than only appearing to. Intended path: open renewal negotiation with the incumbent armed with market benchmarks, targeting price and payment-term concessions toward the 18% cut, and revisit second-sourcing next cycle once supply continuity is secured.
